digest.component_or_area: Plan-review criterion T1 web-search capability gating
propositions: T1, a blocking plan-review criterion requiring web-search grounding, lost access to Anthropic's server-side web_search tool after cutover to Bedrock because the gating logic matched provider-name prefix 'anthropic' rather than querying capability registry membership.
The prefix-match gate in _anthropic_web_search_capabilities violates the epic's zero-exceptions rule that provider qualification must derive from registry membership, not name shape.
The silent loss of web access left no audit trail in signed verdicts; provider_provenance.capabilities did not record whether web grounding was attached, making the degradation undetectable.

Web access must be guaranteed on every provider rebar routes T1 to, including Bedrock, by routing to native Anthropic server-side tool where available and falling back to local DuckDuckGo search where not.
The decision to gate web access must not inspect provider or model name strings; it must derive solely from model profile membership in the capability registry, consistent with epic requirements.

The rubric for T1 must assert web access as a guaranteed property, not a conditional fallback, while retaining explicit prohibitions on fabricated citations and framing results as untrusted input to a blocking gate.
